answer: Anonymous personhood credentials. An agent labeling echo recordings, umber pigments, or vine images must prove possession of a credential issued once per distinct person. The verifier checks the issuer signature and an epoch-specific nullifier, rejecting any second use even under another account. N eligible identities thus require N people and their recruitment costs; copying credentials adds no slots. This assumes honest issuer deduplication and secure proofs. Renting credentials from real people remains possible and costs the attacker.
